title: ksqlDB Basics
description: Query and transform Kafka streams in real time using ksqlDB's SQL-like syntax.

data.text: **ksqlDB** is a streaming SQL engine for Apache Kafka that lets you build real-time applications and pipelines using a SQL-like language. Instead of writing Java code, you define **streams** and **tables** with CREATE STREAM and CREATE TABLE statements, then run continuous queries that process data as it arrives. ksqlDB is ideal for teams that want stream processing without maintaining a custom application.

In ksqlDB, a **stream** is an unbounded sequence of events, similar to a Kafka topic. A **table** is a view of the latest value for each key in a stream, backed by a compacted Kafka topic. You can create a stream from an existing topic or declare a new topic inline, and you can derive a table from a stream using an aggregation query.

terms.definition: An ordered, immutable sequence of events in ksqlDB, mapped to a Kafka topic.
A view of the latest record per key, backed by a compacted Kafka topic.
A ksqlDB query that runs forever, processing new records as they arrive.
A one-time query that returns the current result set, similar to a traditional database SELECT.

data.title: Create a Click Stream
data.content: The following ksqlDB statements create a stream from a Kafka topic and run a continuous aggregation.
data.code:
CREATE STREAM click_events (
  url VARCHAR,
  user_id VARCHAR,
  timestamp VARCHAR
) WITH (
  KAFKA_TOPIC = 'clicks',
  VALUE_FORMAT = 'JSON',
  TIMESTAMP = 'timestamp'
);

CREATE TABLE clicks_per_url AS
  SELECT url,
    COUNT(*) AS total_clicks
  FROM click_events
  WINDOW TUMBLING (SIZE 1 MINUTE)
  GROUP BY url;

-- Push query for current results
SELECT * FROM clicks_per_url EMIT CHANGES;

data.text: While ksqlDB has its own REST API and CLI, .NET applications typically interact with ksqlDB results by consuming the output topics using the **Confluent.Kafka** client. You can also call the ksqlDB REST API directly from C# to push queries and retrieve results.

data.content: Read aggregated click counts from a Kafka topic using the Confluent.Kafka client.

data.title: ksqlDB Server Mode
data.text: ksqlDB runs as a server with a REST endpoint on port 8088. You can send CREATE, DROP, and SELECT statements via HTTP POST to /ksql, making it easy to integrate with external tools and CI pipelines.

data.caption: ksqlDB query processing pipeline
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Topic[(Kafka Topic: clicks)] --> KS[ksqlDB Server]
    KS -->|CREATE STREAM| Stream[Click Stream]
    Stream -->|CREATE TABLE AS| Table[Clicks Per URL]
    Table -->|Push Query| UI[Dashboard / API]
    Table -->|Compact| OutTopic[(Output Topic)]
    style KS fill:#f9f,stroke:#333,stroke-width:2px

items.question: Does ksqlDB support joins?
items.answer: Yes. ksqlDB supports stream-stream, stream-table, and table-table joins, including windowed joins. You specify the join condition in the SELECT statement.

items.question: Can I use ksqlDB with schema registry?
items.answer: Absolutely. ksqlDB integrates with Confluent Schema Registry for Avro, Protobuf, and JSON Schema formats, ensuring data contracts are enforced.

items.question: What happens if the ksqlDB server restarts?
items.answer: ksqlDB recovers its internal state from Kafka changelog topics and resumes processing from the last committed offset. Queries are re-established automatically.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ksqlDB lets you write stream processing logic in SQL
CREATE STREAM maps to a Kafka topic; CREATE TABLE maps to a compacted topic
Push queries return live results; pull queries return point-in-time snapshots
Consume ksqlDB results from any language via standard Kafka consumers
data.takeaway: ksqlDB is the fastest way to get started with stream processing when your team prefers SQL over application code.

data.title: Exercise: Query Streams with ksqlDB
data.description: Set up ksqlDB, create a stream from a Kafka topic, and build a continuously updating table of event counts per category.
steps: Start ksqlDB server in Docker with `docker run -p 8088:8088 confluentinc/ksqldb-server`
Open the ksqlDB CLI or REST API
Create a stream for an existing topic with JSON-encoded events
Write a CREATE TABLE AS query that counts events per category in 5-minute windows
Run a push query to verify live results, then consume from the output topic in C#
data.expectedOutcome: A running ksqlDB query that maintains a live count of events per category
